mainChanges: Forge previews exact per-item stats for all six faces and five equipment slots, true balance and cap reasons, without spending RNG or changing upgrade rules.
Forge-only responsive layout and native details retain the existing visual system and offline assets.
Spring choices and new outcomes explain shield top-up floors and preservation of a stronger existing shield; resolved history stays unchanged.
Reject malformed healing offers before import archives or current saves can be replaced; normal merchant and black-market purchases remain valid.
Current V5 decoding removes one redundant clone while retaining full validation, snapshot conflicts, mirrored saving, legacy migrations and public migrateSave copy semantics.

Only the first JavaScript animation sample is calibrated; later time gaps use actual elapsed time. Lifecycle cancellation, deadline, skip and cleanup release all waiters. The measured all-gap slow-motion candidate was rolled back.
regressionGuards: Schema 5 and all original persistent keys, V1–V4 migrations and original V4 equipment IDs remain.
Manual rolls of up to six dice, six-room floors, one weapon/armor/three relics, one gold currency, eight rarities and depth gates remain.
No enemy/boss statistics, drop probabilities, prices, RNG algorithms, fusion math, nextLuck lifetime or talent rules were changed.
All 29 input test files retained: 28 byte-identical; effects.test only adapts its import loader and retains every old assertion.
Eight offline font/license files, all original artwork/CSS and dice-renderer.js remain byte-identical. No runtime raster assets or dependencies added.

testSummary.deepScope: Fresh-game legal engine policies, 6 x 200 and 2 x 400; not human win rate or matched-path policy causation.

performance.finalRendererScope: 3840x2160 Boss full, fresh Chromium per window, whole-version SwiftShader diagnostic
performance.conclusion: 10k in-memory storage timings improve; 1k save p50 regresses. Final renderer has two worse p95 pairs and worse maximum; no general FPS gain.

packaging.finalArchiveRule: After candidate evidence is added, the unique final ZIP is built and verified/extracted again with syntax/core/owned HTTP. Final ZIP bytes/SHA/file count are external, never its own embedded self-hash.

openRisks: P2 rendering: final software 4K sample still has 1.5–2.7s RAF gaps; two of three p95 pairs worsen and worst max increases. First-sample correction does not prevent later stalls skipping intermediate effects.
P2 economy/build evidence: 400-floor policies retain about 1.46m/1.49m gold; thirty same-opening forge branches do not yet prove a survival gain.
P2 large saves: full snapshots remain synchronous; Node memory Storage is not browser disk or quota latency, and 1k full-save p50 regresses.
P3 fusion: scrollable hover details can cover adjacent cards; initial native-click failures and the separately verified dismissal path are preserved. No production fusion redesign this round.
NOT_TESTED: physical GPU/4K, Windows double-click, real phone/touch, audio listening, external screen reader and real OS/power-loss behavior.
nextRoundPriorities: Profile real GPU and controlled software stalls without reducing visual recipes by default.
Test deep economy opportunity costs and representative builds with actual pressure and more seeds.
Improve fusion tooltip dismissal/placement and narrow-screen usability with direct interaction evidence.
Profile full browser large-save latency while preserving snapshot/mirror/legacy safety.
evidenceNotes: All round04 counts are fresh executions, not copied historical passes.
The entire all-gap candidate was not shipped; its 62+6 negative windows and minimal old clock source remain clearly marked.
Deterministic Node tests reproduce both original first-frame defects; the final browser baseline cases did not reproduce them in that run.
Full-gate source hashes were stable. Later changes are confined to two QA drivers, not game production or unit-test assertions. Their failed attempts are preserved.
Imported malformed saves, quota, RAF and visibility cases are synthetic; naturally generated corruption or physical hardware behavior are not inferred.
Generated original forge art was explored and rejected as an unnecessary runtime bitmap; existing 3D/CSS/fonts carry the shipped UI.
